parsed.explanation: The combined national/division regime has tier-1 visitor exposures: binary birth-sex passports/visas, border fraud screening, document invalidation, and birth-sex facility bans covering airports/public buildings. Division law adds fines, arrest risk and private bounty suits; custody reports include severe abuse. Family/minor travel is worse because care bans, school/provider investigations and disclosure risks are operative. Protective laws, injunctions and marriage/employment rights are resident-facing or unproven for visitors, not offsets. No execution and penalties usually monetary/short detention keep it above 0.15 anchors, but universal exposure with weak recourse places it at lower High Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: National passports/visas enforce binary birth sex; discrepancies can trigger refusal, evidence demands, permanent fraud findings, detention or stranding. Division invalidates birth-mismatched licences, increasing ID-check mismatch risk.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; no documented visitor safe passage; lawsuit unresolved.
entry_documents.interaction: Border screening can out a traveller, then state facility checks or ID invalidation amplify exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse. National corrections bureau adopted policies removing hormones and substituting psychiatric treatment; a documented national-pattern restroom arrest included men's-ward placement.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented operating visitor custody protection; injunctions/lawsuits unresolved.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document mismatch or facility dispute can lead to police or immigration custody with birth-sex placement risk.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars birth-mismatched facility access in government-funded single-sex sites. Division law confines trans people to birth-sex facilities in airports, schools and offices, adding fines, criminal/civil penalties and private bounty lawsuits.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State anti-discrimination/public-accommodation laws exist but are not documented as operating against the facility ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal funding/facility policy plus division law make public-building use continuous exposure.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care for minors is banned across many units, public insurance reimbursement is blocked, youth crisis services ended, and providers/schools can face investigations or funding loss.
care_services.protection: No documented safe care pathway for visitors; local bans/injunctions not shown operative for travelling families.
care_services.interaction: A minor or adult continuity-care need can produce refusal, disclosure, or provider/guardian scrutiny.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism language frames radically pro-transgender ideology as hostile, while directives target schools promoting gender identity and threaten prosecution of facilitators of minor social transition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Not documented that authorities treat trans visitors neutrally; national bias-crime coverage remains partial.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing supports stops, facility enforcement, bounty suits and fear of reporting.

minors_guardians.exposure: Travelling minors face birth-sex facility rules, care denial, school investigations and disclosure risks; guardians or providers may face inquiry, funding loss or penalties for affirming identity.
minors_guardians.protection: Same-sex marriage/adoption and municipal conversion bans are resident-oriented or not shown operative for visitors.
minors_guardians.interaction: Entry mismatch can combine with school/care contacts to out the child and burden guardians.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No traveler-specific violence rate is documented, but facility disputes can invite arrest, fines and lawsuits, and hostile custody placement is reported.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime law covers gender identity, but state coverage omits it and visitor enforcement is unshown.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police or bystander suits may escalate social friction into legal jeopardy; reporting risk uncertain.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Lawsuits/injunctions are unresolved; border, enforcement and victim counts are missing. Federal, division, municipal and tribal layers make rules changeable.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid FAQ gives advice but no documented effective visitor remedy; courts are not shown to promptly relieve harms.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Uncertainty prevents relying on protective law; the harshest operative federal/state rule controls.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.15-A involves public-decency arrest, months of pretrial custody, guard violence and capital ambiguity. The dossier lacks documented execution and likely months-long visitor custody, but has comparable immigration/corrections abuse and facility criminalisation, so the rating should sit above 0.15 but below protective anchors.

0.25-C has birth-sex prison placement, cross-dressing arrests, short sentences and no execution. This jurisdiction matches those severity drivers and adds universal airport/public-building restrictions, ID invalidation and private bounty lawsuits, with unresolved remedies, making 0.24 a defensible lower-edge High Risk score.

0.75-C permits markers matching presentation, trained border officers, brief secondary checks and reliable release. This jurisdiction does the opposite: national passport/visa binary screening, birth-sex facility bans and hostile custody/care rules, so it is far below 0.75 despite court litigation.

parsed.synthesis: Federal document and border rules make mismatch likely and create entry refusal or stranding; division facility and ID rules make airports, offices and police checks unavoidable. Because private bounty suits do not require prosecutors, enforcement can arise from any bystander, raising exposure beyond arrest statistics. Custody and care rules convert a bathroom or continuity-care need into possible humiliation, abuse, or denial. Unresolved lawsuits and partial state protections are not documented operational shields, so a traveller experiences the harshest federal-plus-division rules as controlling.
